title: Brandhub
role: Software Engineer II · The Branding Club
summary: Full-stack and AI engineering on Brandhub: business workflows, Python/Django APIs, PostgreSQL data and a company-data LLM assistant.
metrics: less manual content effort · team outcome
overview: At The Branding Club, I work as a Software Engineer II on Brandhub, a production B2B SaaS platform serving more than 8,000 brands. My work connects Next.js and TypeScript interfaces with Python/Django services and PostgreSQL, alongside AI features that help users get answers from their business data.
challenge: Orders, billing, stock and finance depend on the same business records, so a change in one workflow can affect several others. My work is to make these flows clear and reliable, integrate their APIs, and give the LLM assistant relevant company context without exposing records outside the user’s access.
built: Build and maintain ordering, billing, finance and customer-portal features, working from requirements through implementation, debugging and release.
Develop Next.js, React and TypeScript interfaces with reusable components, forms, tables and Redux state. Handle loading, validation and API failures within each workflow.
Work across Python/Django REST APIs and PostgreSQL-backed services, including data integration, authentication and role-based access.
Built an LLM assistant for questions about company data. RAG and vector retrieval bring relevant context into the request so answers can use business records.
Integrate OpenAI and Gemini APIs and work on prompts, context handling and agentic workflows, with review points for generated output.
Contributed to AI-assisted content workflows that reduced manual content effort by 70% as a team outcome.
Improved page-load time by 50% and achieved Lighthouse scores above 90 through frontend performance work.
Collaborate with designers, backend engineers and business stakeholders, review changes and use AI coding tools to support implementation and debugging.
tradeoff: For the assistant, the important boundary is which data can enter the prompt and what the user can act on afterward. For application features, I focus on clear state, reusable components and predictable API behaviour so business users can complete their work.

title: YourKhata
role: Independently built product · Full-stack & AI engineering
summary: An AI-native, multi-tenant business product built with Next.js, Python/Django and PostgreSQL, integrating LLM and RAG workflows with business records.
overview: I’m building YourKhata as an AI-native business product that connects everyday operations with useful assistance grounded in business information. I own product research, Next.js interfaces, Python/Django REST APIs, PostgreSQL data modelling, LLM and RAG integration, and deployment. It supports multiple tenants and multiple businesses, with clear access boundaries between their records.
challenge: The hard part is making records stay consistent across invoices, stock, payments and reports while keeping each business separate. AI adds another requirement: a useful response needs the correct business context, rather than an unrestricted view of all the stored information.
built: Translate business workflows into a product that connects ledgers, invoicing, inventory, purchases, expenses and payments.
Build the backend in Python and Django REST Framework with PostgreSQL, and the web experience in Next.js, React and TypeScript.
Implement multi-tenant and multi-business access, with owner, admin, staff and accountant roles controlling access to records and operations.
Integrate LLM-powered assistance and RAG workflows to retrieve relevant business context and turn questions into useful responses grounded in that information.
Connect AI functionality to the application’s data and permissions so the selected business determines the context available to the assistant.
Build reports, reminders, traceable corrections, statements, import/export and payment-related workflows around the same business records.
Handle Docker-based deployment, scheduled jobs and production configuration, alongside debugging and iteration.
Implement SEO and GEO foundations: discoverable pages, metadata, canonicals, sitemaps, FAQs and structured data. Achieved PageSpeed 99+ on desktop and 90+ on mobile.
tradeoff: I keep the accounting and record-management operations deterministic, while using LLM and RAG capabilities to help people find and understand information. Tenant and business permissions apply to the context supplied to AI as well as the ordinary application workflows.

title: ml-uikit
summary: A published React and TypeScript UI library built on shadcn/ui and Radix, documented in Storybook and used with Next.js applications.
overview: I built ml-uikit to avoid rebuilding the same application controls and interaction patterns. It packages reusable React and TypeScript components on shadcn/ui and Radix foundations, with Storybook documentation and integration into Next.js applications.
challenge: Product teams often rebuild the same controls and interaction patterns. A useful library needs a discoverable API, accessible states, sensible theming and packaging that behaves predictably in consuming applications.
built: Build reusable React and TypeScript components on shadcn/ui and Radix UI, with customizable Tailwind styling.
Cover application needs such as phone, search and date-range inputs, forms, pagination, sidebars, charts and table controls.
Use the components in Next.js applications and keep integration concerns visible in the library’s APIs and documentation.
Document component variants and states in Storybook so consuming developers can explore behaviour before integrating a component.
Add dark-mode support, typed APIs and accessibility-focused component tooling.
Configure ESM/CommonJS packaging, TypeScript declarations, external dependencies and tree-shaking, then publish the library on npm.
tradeoff: I reuse established primitives for the interaction foundations and focus my work on the APIs, documentation and product controls that consuming applications need.

title: Aira
summary: A user-controlled memory layer that helps AI tools work from consistent preferences, projects and decisions.
overview: Aira is a memory and context layer for AI tools. It organizes information into user-controlled records so an assistant can retrieve relevant context without treating raw conversation history as canonical memory.
challenge: AI tools often repeat questions or lose important decisions between sessions. A useful memory system needs to preserve provenance, handle changed or superseded facts, respect privacy boundaries, and fit relevant context into a limited token budget.
built: Designed a provider-independent core with REST, MCP and hooks as integration surfaces.
Implemented typed, scoped and versioned memory records with provenance, confidence, supersession and an auditable lifecycle.
Kept raw conversations separate from canonical memory and filtered disallowed scopes before retrieval.
Built a retrieval pipeline combining SQLite FTS5 and vector search, with candidate fusion, ranking, diversification and token-budgeted context assembly.
Added explicit grants, private sessions and reviewable context-injection logs.
tradeoff: Prioritizes portable memory and inspectable context first; broader integrations and sync are staged behind the core privacy and retrieval model.

title: Generative AI Job-Application Assistant
summary: Turns a candidate profile and job description into structured fit notes and tailored application drafts.
overview: A generative AI assistant for organizing candidate information, role requirements and application materials. It helps produce useful drafts while leaving review and submission decisions with the candidate.
challenge: Job applications involve repeated comparisons between the same work history and many role descriptions. The system should reduce repetitive writing while keeping facts traceable to the candidate profile and avoiding unsupported claims.
built: Created workflows to organize candidate profiles, resume variants, job descriptions and application tracking.
Added LLM-powered profile-to-role comparison with structured fit and skill-gap summaries.
Generated tailored responses and role-specific documents for candidate review.
Used configurable model-provider integration, validation and editable, candidate-controlled profile data.
Kept application review and submission under the candidate’s control.
tradeoff: Optimizes for transparent drafts that a candidate can edit, rather than automatic applications that can misstate experience or preferences.

title: Bug Buster
summary: A Jira-connected assistant that analyzes bug context and sends a report with suggested fixes.
overview: Bug Buster connects Jira issue context with an OpenAI-powered analysis workflow to make bug investigation more repeatable for developers.
challenge: Bug reports can be incomplete or spread across issue details and discussion. Developers spend time collecting context before they can identify likely causes and next steps.
built: Connected Jira issue data and relevant context to an OpenAI analysis workflow.
Generated a structured report with likely causes and suggested fixes when a bug was reported.
Automated the repetitive handoff from issue creation to an investigation summary.
Kept engineers responsible for reviewing suggestions and validating any code changes.
tradeoff: Automates context gathering and first-pass analysis, not the final decision to change or ship code.

title: Sci-WebHub

overview: Sci-WebHub provides backend services for build and deployment workflows connected to GitHub repositories.
challenge: A project deployment flow needs to coordinate builds, environment settings, logs and version history without losing track of what was shipped.
built: Built API services for project builds and environment configuration.
Created database workflows to track deployments, logs and version history.
Connected repository-based build steps to deployment records.
tradeoff: Track build configuration, logs and deployment versions together so a release can be traced back to the project and repository workflow that produced it.
